blocking.fix: In §§7.3/10, extend isolation to the newly shared models. Recommended rule: "At bennett_run, the run atomically acquires exclusive ownership of every console, clock and block model referenced by its entry's transitive CC/R call closure. Ownership lasts until CLOSED, including while COMPLETED, FAILED or REVERSED. If any required model is owned by another non-CLOSED run, bennett_run returns E_INVALID_STATE before executing the entry or acquiring ownership. Entropy positions and effect tapes remain per-run. Disjoint concurrent runs require disjoint model ownership sets as well as the existing register/memory conditions." Clarify §14.3: "Restoration concerns the run-owned state; state belonging exclusively to disjoint runs is unaffected." Add a §15 vector: after A reads clock 0 and completes without closing, B's conflicting launch returns E_INVALID_STATE, c remains 1 and B has no effects; after A closes, a new B reads 1, or reads 0 if A first reversed. A viable alternative is dynamic per-model ownership acquired at the first effect, retained until CLOSED, with a conflicting effect producing atomic terminal code 4; that alternative also needs an explicit §4.9 mapping. I recommend launch-time acquisition because it uses the existing launch-conflict status and prevents partial execution before discovering a model conflict.
